title: Data-Driven Discovery of Interpretable Kalman Filter Variants through Large Language Models and Genetic Programming

mechanism.domainTask: data-driven discovery of interpretable state-estimation algorithms
mechanism.populationDetail: Each modality has four independent islands with local top-solution databases; weak islands are periodically reseeded within that modality.
mechanism.archiveDetail: Each island retains a database of the 200 highest-scoring candidate algorithms.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Two distinct representation spaces run in parallel with the same scoring interface; no CGP-to-LLM candidate exchange occurs.
mechanism.generationDetail: LLM prompts combine or mutate two sampled functions; the separate CGP branch mutates one sampled graph by changing edges or node types.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Candidate database stores scalar fitness values for softmax parent sampling; no additional per-candidate evaluator metadata or critique is described.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: LLM prompts use two selected functions and CGP mutation uses one graph; both sample from local databases with fitness-softmax probabilities.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/Data-Driven Discovery of Interpretable Kalman Filter Variants through Large Language Models and Genetic Programming.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Current survey cites only island population and open-source ecosystem. Paper's code footnote says URL will be added upon publication, so release claim needs external verification. Fixed temperature/island reset should not be called adaptive; shared fitness must not imply cross-modality candidate exchange. LLM mutation locality is unspecified.
